headline: Sandy Hook starter pack.
subhead: A quick guide to landmarks, parks, and water access. Swipe.

slides.title: Sandy Hook Village
slides.text: The walkable commercial center along the Pootatuck River connects local shops, sidewalks, and the annual holiday tree lighting.

slides.title: Eichler's Cove Marina
slides.text: Town-owned public access to Lake Zoar featuring a boat launch, public beach, and seasonal boat slips.

slides.title: Paugussett State Forest
slides.text: Miles of marked hiking trails across Upper and Lower parcels, running along the ridge above Lake Housatonic.

slides.title: Treadwell Memorial Park
slides.text: A municipal park offering athletic fields, tennis courts, picnic pavilions, and a town swimming pool.

slides.title: Interstate 84 Access
slides.text: Exits 10 and 11 provide direct east-west highway travel toward Danbury, Waterbury, and Route 34 connections.

slides.title: Village Tree Lighting
slides.text: A long-standing annual late-fall gathering held right near the river bridge in the village center.

caption:
Eichler's Cove and the trails in Paugussett State Forest show how much water access defines Sandy Hook CT.

Most people know Sandy Hook for its village center along the Pootatuck River. It is easy to walk, and Interstate 84 sits right at Exits 10 and 11 for highway travel toward Danbury or Hartford.

If you head east toward Lake Zoar, you get town boat launches, quiet trailheads, and municipal recreation at Treadwell Park. As November winds down, the annual village tree lighting gets underway.
